tasks.title: Define shared array and fitted-state validation
tasks.summary: Create reusable validation for observation matrices, targets, finite values, feature counts, and fitted-state checks without hiding estimator-specific assumptions.
acceptance: Validation errors name the violated shape or state contract.
Tests cover empty, one-dimensional, mismatched, non-finite, and valid inputs.
The API remains usable by regression, classification, transformation, and clustering implementations.

tasks.title: Build the common experiment runner
tasks.summary: Run compatible estimators without leaking evaluation data and return structured, serializable experiment evidence.
acceptance: Train, validation, and final test boundaries are explicit.
Preprocessing is fitted only on the training partition.
Results record estimator parameters, data identity, random state, metrics, and timing.
Tests detect a deliberately leaky preprocessing path.

tasks.title: Implement cross-validation and model-selection utilities
tasks.summary: Implement deterministic splitters and parameter search that preserve evaluation boundaries and expose all selection evidence.
acceptance: K-fold and stratified behavior are defined and tested.
Randomness is reproducible without mutating NumPy global state.
Parameter search reports every evaluated candidate, not only the winner.
Differential tests compare compatible cases with scikit-learn.

tasks.title: Expand task-aware evaluation metrics
tasks.summary: Provide regression, classification, probabilistic, and clustering metrics with explicit edge-case conventions.
acceptance: Each metric documents orientation, range, units, and undefined cases.
Tests use hand-computable examples, boundaries, and trusted-library comparisons.
Aggregation never silently mixes incompatible tasks or units.

tasks.title: Implement linear regression through stable numerical methods
tasks.summary: Implement intercept handling, least-squares fitting, prediction, and diagnostics without explicitly inverting the normal-equation matrix.
acceptance: The derivation connects the objective, gradient, and least-squares solution.
Rank-deficient and poorly conditioned designs have explicit behavior.
Tests include exact lines, multiple features, rank deficiency, and scikit-learn comparison.
Residual and fitted attributes follow the common platform conventions.

tasks.title: Implement reusable gradient-based optimization
tasks.summary: Implement batch and mini-batch gradient descent with reproducible sampling, stopping criteria, histories, and numerical checks.
acceptance: Finite-difference tests validate supplied gradients on smooth objectives.
Learning-rate, iteration, tolerance, and divergence behavior are explicit.
Histories expose objective and gradient-norm evidence without unbounded memory growth.
A linear-regression example agrees with a least-squares reference.

tasks.title: Implement binary logistic regression
tasks.summary: Implement numerically stable probabilities, regularized log loss, fitting, decision scores, and thresholded predictions.
acceptance: Logistic loss and sigmoid calculations remain stable for extreme scores.
Regularization excludes or explicitly documents treatment of the intercept.
Tests cover label validation, probabilities, separable data, and trusted-library comparison.
Threshold choice is separate from probability estimation.

tasks.title: Implement k-nearest-neighbor estimators
tasks.summary: Implement classification and regression with explicit distance, weighting, tie, and scaling contracts.
acceptance: Invalid k, dimension mismatch, ties, and zero-distance neighbors have documented behavior.
Tests include hand-computable geometry and scikit-learn comparisons.
The documentation explains why preprocessing belongs outside the estimator.

tasks.title: Implement decision-tree learning
tasks.summary: Implement a bounded classification or regression tree with deterministic split selection and inspectable nodes.
acceptance: Impurity, candidate splits, stopping rules, and tie-breaking are mathematically specified.
Constant features, repeated values, depth limits, and minimum samples are tested.
The fitted tree can be inspected without relying on private recursive state.
Small cases receive differential comparison with scikit-learn.

tasks.title: Implement a random-forest ensemble
tasks.summary: Build reproducible bootstrap aggregation and feature subsampling over the class-built tree implementation.
acceptance: Every source of randomness derives from a documented local generator.
Bootstrap membership and out-of-bag evidence are inspectable.
Aggregation and classification ties are deterministic.
Tests demonstrate variance reduction on a fixed real dataset.

tasks.title: Implement a boosting ensemble
tasks.summary: Implement one explicitly chosen boosting algorithm with inspectable stage weights and failure behavior.
acceptance: The chosen loss and update equations are derived and documented.
Degenerate weak learners and numerical weight normalization are handled.
Stage-wise predictions and training histories are inspectable.
Tests compare small cases and trends with a trusted implementation.

tasks.title: Implement a multilayer neural network
tasks.summary: Implement forward propagation, reverse-mode gradients, training, and prediction for a bounded dense network.
acceptance: Tensor shapes and parameter initialization are explicit and validated.
Finite-difference checks validate layer and loss gradients.
Randomness, batching, stopping, and loss histories are reproducible.
A real-data example separates optimization evidence from final evaluation.

tasks.title: Implement principal component analysis
tasks.summary: Implement centered PCA through a stable decomposition with transforms, inverse transforms, and explained-variance evidence.
acceptance: Centering, component orientation ambiguity, and rank limits are documented.
Tests use known covariance structure, reconstruction properties, and scikit-learn comparison.
The implementation avoids an unnecessary covariance matrix when SVD is appropriate.

tasks.title: Implement k-means clustering
tasks.summary: Implement reproducible initialization, assignment, centroid updates, convergence evidence, and prediction.
acceptance: Initialization and empty-cluster behavior are explicit.
Inertia is non-increasing across accepted update steps.
Multiple restarts are reproducible and select the documented optimum.
Tests account for permutation invariance of cluster labels.

tasks.title: Implement agglomerative hierarchical clustering
tasks.summary: Implement selected linkage criteria with an inspectable merge history and explicit distance conventions.
acceptance: Linkage definitions and tie-breaking are mathematically specified.
The merge history has valid monotone structure for supported linkages.
Hand-computable and trusted-library comparisons cover small datasets.
Complexity limitations are honest and measured.

tasks.title: Implement density-based clustering
tasks.summary: Implement a density-based method with explicit neighborhood, border, core, and noise semantics.
acceptance: Boundary conventions for radius comparisons are explicit.
Cluster labels are tested modulo permutation and noise identity.
Tests cover all-noise, one-cluster, border-point, and trusted-library cases.

tasks.title: Define model cards and experiment provenance
tasks.summary: Create a serializable evidence record connecting data identity, code revision, package release, estimator parameters, metrics, and limitations.
acceptance: Records are deterministic, schema-versioned, and free of secrets or private records.
Required provenance cannot be omitted silently.
A final-product template can render the record without importing notebook state.

tasks.title: Connect model behavior to production monitoring
tasks.summary: Define structured prediction events and delayed-quality evidence that final products can monitor without logging sensitive features.
acceptance: The event schema separates operational, data-quality, and model-quality signals.
Sensitive raw observations are excluded by design.
Tests cover schema evolution, missing delayed labels, and aggregation boundaries.
The production monitoring laboratory demonstrates the contract.
